I don't know if you can say we "choose" not to. I have never owned an iPhone, but I know that the reason for jailbreaking is to "backdoor" unauthorized applications. It's a method of installing standalone packages... but Apple keeps shutting down jailbreak avenues.

Sure, we could take a stand and stop buying iDevices, but that's pretty unreasonable on a global scale, when they're one of two major mobile competitors.

I'd say we're strong-armed into this predicament... you either sell your usage to Google, or you lose backporting apps on an iDevice, or you hate everything about life with Windows Mobile. There's really no quality alternative out there right now.

Not natively. I mean, technically you can, but you'll need to have certifications, the company making the app needs an enterprise license. If you jailbreak (which everyone should), you can download and install whatever the hell you want

Both. Android (Vanilla at least), Ubuntu, and any number of other Linux flavors have software centers and the ability to install whatever you want. Windows does it now too, as well as Apple computers.

There are definite advantages to both systems. Freedom to install anything allows for super small developers to get their stuff out there and people to discover software from anywhere. And this software isn't held to the same standards of IP law, so things that wouldn't fly on app stores can happen (Fan Games, Emulators, etc.)

Likewise, app stores have different advantages: For users, they trust the software that is on the app store because it's seen as safer (and it generally is, but not 100% safe all the time). For developers, it enables another avenue for discovery. Finally, an easy way to pay that doesn't expose payment information to random people on the internet is mostly good for both parties involved.
I like the no-malware guarantee I get with the iOS App Store. I also like the flexibility to run whatever I want on Windows (and I can just sandbox stuff on a VM). Horses for courses.
